AI.tldr: Stellar rotation reduces core temperature and ALP emission in supernovae, weakening energy-loss constraints on axion-like particles from SN 1987A, while gamma-ray limits remain unchanged.
AI.motivation: To understand how stellar rotation influences constraints on MeV-scale axion-like particles (ALPs) from SN 1987A observations.
AI.method: Two-dimensional core-collapse supernova simulations with varying initial angular velocities in the iron core for different progenitor models; post-processing to estimate ALP emission rates.
AI.result: Rotation suppresses ALP emission more than neutrino luminosity by lowering core temperature via centrifugal support, relaxing energy-loss constraints especially in the rotating 18 solar mass model; gamma-ray constraints remain largely unaffected by rotation due to their dependence on the ALP-photon coupling.
AI.conclusion: Stellar rotation relaxes the energy-loss-based constraints on ALP parameters from SN 1987A by reducing ALP emission, although gamma-ray limits stay robust; constraints are sensitive to temporal evaluation and progenitor models.

title: In-depth analysis of the clustering of dark matter particles around primordial black holes. Part III: CMB constraints
summary: In a mixed dark matter scenario in which primordial black holes (PBHs) would co-exist with thermally produced self-annihilating particles, one expects the former to be surrounded by extremely dense halos made of the latter, built up during radiation domination. Here, as a continuation of previous work, we derive observational limits on such a scenario from a full statistical analysis of cosmic microwave background (CMB) data. We quantify how a tiny fraction $\fbh$ of PBHs could restrict the parameter space available to thermal particle dark matter, limiting the $s$-wave annihilation cross section to values $\lesssim 10^{-30}\,{\rm cm^3/s}\,(\mchi/100\,{\rm GeV})\,(\fbh/10^{-6})^{-3}$ if PBHs are typically heavier than $\sim 10^{-10}\,\Msun$, which can also be turned into constraints on PBHs in this mass range. In contrast, asteroid mass or lighter PBHs could live in perfect peace with these particles. Finally, we shortly discuss the implications of the recent tentative interpretation of Subaru-HSC microlensing events as PBHs.

AI.tldr: This paper uses CMB data to set limits on dark matter models where primordial black holes coexist with self-annihilating particles, finding that heavier PBHs strongly constrain annihilation rates, while lighter ones do not, with implications for recent PBH microlensing observations.
AI.motivation: Investigate the interplay between primordial black holes (PBHs) and thermally produced self-annihilating particle dark matter in a mixed dark matter scenario during radiation domination.
AI.method: Perform a full statistical analysis of cosmic microwave background (CMB) data to derive observational limits on the coexistence of PBHs and self-annihilating particle dark matter halos.
AI.result: Establish stringent constraints on the thermal particle dark matter annihilation cross-section dependent on PBH fraction and mass, notably that for PBHs heavier than ~10^-10 solar masses, the annihilation cross section must be below ~10^-30 cm^3/s scaled by mass and PBH fraction; lighter PBHs face no such constraints. Also discuss implications for recent Subaru-HSC microlensing PBH candidate events.
AI.conclusion: A small fraction of PBHs can significantly restrict the parameter space for thermal self-annihilating particle dark matter by limiting their annihilation cross section, particularly for heavier PBHs, thus providing constraints on both dark matter models and PBH properties.

title: Superfluid $^3$He aerogel experiments as a laboratory neutron star analogue
summary: Neutron stars make a unique astrophysical test bench for our understanding of quantum physics at kilometre scales. The rotation of a neutron star features glitches, sudden spin-ups that interrupt the otherwise regular stellar spin-down, which are often attributed to the dynamics of pinned quantised vortices in one or several of the superfluid phases inside the star. Laboratory experiments probing superfluid vortices have inspired neutron star theory and simulations from the beginning. Here we argue that vortex experiments in superfluids contained in aerogels show phenomenology that offers a highly appealing but vastly unexplored analogue for neutron star physics. We build a point-vortex simulation that allows analysing experiments in a crust-like and a core-like aerogel, extracting two different regimes of pinned vortex (non-)dynamics and validating a microscopic picture of very strong vortex pinning. In the crust-like aerogel, vortices get depinned once the ambient superflow is fast enough, while in the core-like aerogel pinned vortices are never released and rotational velocity changes are accommodated by the avalanche-like production of new vortices instead. Finally, we show that these concepts should apply also in neutron stars and may thus revolutionise the analysis of neutron star observations.

AI.tldr: This paper models superfluid vortex dynamics in aerogels as analogues to neutron star interiors, revealing distinct pinning behaviors that can explain neutron star glitch phenomena and could revolutionize astrophysical analyses.
AI.motivation: To find analogues in terrestrial superfluid vortex experiments that can illuminate the complex vortex dynamics in neutron stars, facilitating better understanding of glitch phenomena in stellar spin behavior.
AI.method: Construction of a point-vortex simulation to analyze superfluid vortex behavior in two types of aerogel environments (crust-like and core-like), extracting distinct regimes of vortex pinning and dynamics.
AI.result: Identification of two vortex dynamics regimes: in crust-like aerogel, vortices depin upon sufficient superflow; in core-like aerogel, vortices remain pinned and rotational changes are handled via vortex avalanches. These provide a validated microscopic model of strong vortex pinning relevant to neutron stars.
AI.conclusion: Vortex behavior observed in superfluid aerogel experiments offers a compelling and previously underutilized analogue to neutron star physics, potentially transforming the interpretation of neutron star glitch data and advancing quantum physics understanding at astrophysical scales.

title: A barotropic alternative to Early Dark Energy for alleviating the $H_0$ tension
comment: 25 pages, 13 figures, 9 tables. Comments are welcome
summary: We propose a cosmological scenario in which, beyond matter and radiation, an additional barotropic fluid with positive equation of state $ω_s$ contributes to the cosmic energy budget, in contrast to Early Dark Energy (EDE). We investigate the theoretical implications of this framework, here dubbed the $Λ_{ω_s}$CDM model, at both the background and perturbative levels, exploring its impact on the expansion history and structure formation. We show that, while remaining subdominant at late times and therefore consistent with current observational bounds, the additional fluid modifies the early-time expansion rate, leading to a higher inferred value of the Hubble constant. Thus, we perform a full Bayesian analysis using a modified version of the \texttt{CLASS} Boltzmann code interfaced with \texttt{MontePython}, considering combinations of \textit{Planck} 2018 Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data, DESI DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) measurements, Pantheon Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), and SH0ES determinations of $H_0$. We find that the inclusion of the SH0ES prior, $H_0 = 73.04 \pm 1.04\,\mathrm{km/s/Mpc}$, leads to a preference for a nonvanishing barotropic fluid. In particular, we obtain $ω_s = 0.290^{+0.017(0.021)}_{-0.007(0.028)}$ and density $10^5Ω_s = 1.47^{+0.35(1.14)}_{-0.62(0.94)}$ for the dataset combination CMB + BAO + Pantheon + SH0ES, and $ω_s = 0.302^{+0.024(0.034)}_{-0.013(0.038)}$ and $10^5Ω_s = 1.21^{+0.31(1.10)}_{-0.65(0.86)}$ when BAO data are excluded. We further compare our scenario with the EDE framework and show that, statistically, no strong evidence is found against the $Λ_{ω_s}$CDM model. Finally, we provide a physical interpretation of our fluid in terms of matter with pressure, indicating that the standard cosmological model may be incomplete in its current minimal formulation.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes adding a positive pressure barotropic fluid to the cosmological model, improving consistency with high local $H_0$ measurements by altering early-universe expansion. Bayesian analysis with current large-scale structure and CMB data finds a statistically viable fit comparable to Early Dark Energy, indicating a potentially incomplete standard model.
AI.motivation: Address the Hubble constant discrepancy by introducing a new cosmological component beyond matter, radiation, and Early Dark Energy.
AI.method: Development of the $Λ_{ω_s}$CDM model incorporating an additional barotropic fluid; theoretical analysis at background and perturbation levels; Bayesian parameter inference using modified CLASS and MontePython codes with datasets from Planck 2018 CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon SNe Ia, and SH0ES $H_0$ prior.
AI.result: The model yields a positive barotropic fluid parameter $ω_s\approx0.29-0.30$ and a small but nonnegligible density contribution, which modifies early-time expansion to increase the inferred $H_0$; fits data comparably to Early Dark Energy with no strong statistical disfavor.
AI.conclusion: Introducing a positive equation of state barotropic fluid provides a viable and physically interpretable extension to standard $\Lambda$CDM that can alleviate the Hubble tension without conflicting with current observations, suggesting incompleteness of the minimal cosmological model.

title: X-Ray Polarization from the Atoll 4U 1735-44 Suggests a Low Inclination
summary: X-ray polarimetry is a new tool capable of probing the geometry of accretion onto weakly magnetized neutron stars. Here we present the first X-ray spectropolarimetric results from coordinated observations of the atoll source 4U 1735-44, conducted with the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE), NICER, and NuSTAR. Over the 2-8 keV energy range, we obtained a marginal detection of polarization with the polarization degree of $1.4\%\pm0.7\%$ and polarization angle of $-29^\circ\pm14^\circ$, corresponding to a $3σ$ upper limit on the polarization degree of 3.5\%. The best-fit model to describe the spectrum comprises a thermal component associated with the accretion disk, a Comptonized blackbody component, and a relativistic reflection component. From the reflection model, we infer a disk inclination of $\sim 40^\circ$. The spectroscopic and polarimetric properties of 4U 1735-44 are consistent with those observed in other atoll sources studied by IXPE, with its low polarization likely due to its low inclination.

AI.tldr: This study presents the first X-ray spectropolarimetric observations of the atoll source 4U 1735-44, revealing marginal polarization consistent with low inclination accretion geometry, confirmed through coordinated IXPE, NICER, and NuSTAR measurements and spectral modeling.
AI.motivation: To utilize X-ray polarimetry to probe the geometry of accretion onto weakly magnetized neutron stars, improving understanding of their emission and structure.
AI.method: Conducted coordinated observations of the atoll source 4U 1735-44 using the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE), NICER, and NuSTAR over the 2-8 keV range, performing spectropolarimetric analyses and spectral modeling including thermal, Comptonized blackbody, and relativistic reflection components.
AI.result: Detected a marginal X-ray polarization degree of 1.4%±0.7%, with a polarization angle of −29°±14°, establishing a 3σ upper limit of 3.5% polarization. Spectral fitting infers a disk inclination around 40°, and the low polarization is consistent with low inclination effects seen in similar sources.
AI.conclusion: The low polarization level detected in 4U 1735-44 supports the notion that atoll sources with low disk inclination exhibit weak polarization signatures, demonstrating that X-ray polarimetry effectively probes accretion geometry in weakly magnetized neutron stars.

title: Galaxy Populations in the IllustrisTNG Caustic Skeleton
summary: The caustic skeleton is a parameter-free and mathematically rigorous formalism for tracing the hierarchical formation history of the multiscale cosmic web from the singularities in the underlying dark matter flow. In the present study, we explicitly use the multistreaming nature of the cosmic mass distribution to address the influence of the weblike embedding on the galaxy populations and discern their properties in different web environments. To this end, we construct the multiscale caustic skeleton of the dark mass distribution in the state-of-the-art suite of the large-scale IllustrisTNG simulations. In addition to the multistreaming dark matter density field, we assess the characteristic properties of the intergalactic baryonic gas in the vicinity of the caustics. Next, we associate the galaxies with the voids, walls, filaments and cluster nodes, and investigate their colours and star formation activities. A unique feature of the analysis is that it explicitly addresses the multiscale aspects with respect to the galaxy population, assessing issues such as the fraction of (blue) galaxies as a function of the scale of the cosmic web pattern and its caustic features. We find that the galaxy properties form a continuum in the scale-space cosmic web. Intimately coupled to the hierarchical build-up of the cosmic structure, it also allows us to systematically assess the impact of the formation time of the various structural components of the cosmic web on the galaxy properties. This furthers insight into the establishment of the observed colour-density relation of galaxies.

AI.tldr: This study uses a parameter-free multiscale formalism to link galaxy properties with their location in the cosmic web, showing that galaxy color and star formation vary continuously with cosmic structure scale and formation history.
AI.motivation: To understand how the multiscale cosmic web structure influences galaxy populations and their properties using a parameter-free, mathematically rigorous approach based on dark matter flow singularities.
AI.method: Using the multistreaming nature of dark matter flow to construct the multiscale caustic skeleton of the dark matter distribution in IllustrisTNG simulations; analyzing intergalactic baryonic gas near caustics; associating galaxies with cosmic web components (voids, walls, filaments, clusters) and examining their colors and star formation activities across scales.
AI.result: Galaxy properties exhibit a continuum across different scales of the cosmic web; the hierarchical formation history of cosmic structures directly impacts galaxy properties such as color and star formation, helping to explain the observed color-density relation of galaxies.
AI.conclusion: The multiscale caustic skeleton method effectively traces the hierarchical cosmic web formation and reveals that galaxy properties are intimately connected with their embedding within the multiscale structures, driven by the formation time and scale of the cosmic web components.

title: Equation of State for warm Neutron Star outer crusts
summary: We describe the equation of state (EoS) of a warm ion plasma as obtained by performing microscopic many-body simulations using Molecular Dynamics computational techniques. Using the cold one-component plasma (OCP) composition in the Neutron Star (NS) outer crust assumed in Murarka et al. (2022) with a representative heavy nucleus for each density, we refine previous calculations. We include electron screening and modeling of ions as finite-size Gaussian distributions in the interaction potential, together with an efficient Ewald energy summation procedure. From this, the EoS relation $P(n_B,T)$ is obtained as a function of baryonic density and temperature in the NS outer crust under conditions $n_B\in[7.48\times 10^{-10},2.09\times10^{-4}]$ $ \rm fm^{-3}$ , $k_{B}T\in[1,5]$ MeV. In order to improve the usability of our results we provide tabulated data values along with a neural network parametrization available in the Zenodo repository, see https://zenodo.org/records/15348712. We find that even at moderate temperatures, thermal effects of ions are key in the higher density region closer to the inner crust, when described using a thermal effective parametrization based on the thermal adiabatic index $Γ_{th}$. We compare our results with other EoS in the literature performing a critical discussion.

AI.tldr: This paper refines the equation of state of warm ion plasma in neutron star outer crusts via Molecular Dynamics simulations that include electron screening and finite-size ion effects. It provides updated EoS data and neural network parametrization, showing the importance of thermal ion effects at moderate temperatures and densities near the inner crust, improving modeling accuracy over previous works.
AI.motivation: To refine the equation of state (EoS) of warm ion plasma in the neutron star outer crust by improving previous models and incorporating thermal and finite-size effects of ions under relevant density and temperature conditions.
AI.method: Performed microscopic many-body Molecular Dynamics simulations using a cold one-component plasma composition with heavy nuclei, incorporating electron screening, finite-size Gaussian ion distributions, and an efficient Ewald energy summation technique to compute the EoS $P(n_B,T)$ as a function of baryonic density and temperature.
AI.result: Obtained a refined EoS relation for baryonic densities in the range $7.48\times10^{-10}$ to $2.09\times10^{-4}\,\rm fm^{-3}$ and temperatures 1–5 MeV, demonstrating significant thermal ion effects at moderate temperatures near the inner crust; provided tabulated data and a neural network parameterization for practical use; results were critically compared with existing literature EoS.
AI.conclusion: Thermal effects of ions significantly influence the EoS in the higher density regions of the neutron star outer crust, necessitating their inclusion for accurate modeling; the refined EoS and parametrization improve upon previous calculations and enhance usability for neutron star studies.

title: The MeerKAT Fornax Survey VII. Characterisation of the Fornax cluster's magnetic field and new insights on magnetisation in large scale systems
summary: Large scale magnetic fields in galaxy clusters can influence their physics and the evolution of the cluster galaxies. These properties remain poorly constrained due to a historical lack of high-sensitivity and high-resolution spectro-polarimetric data. Thanks to the advent of the SKA pathfinders and precursors this is now dramatically changing. By exploiting the densest RM grid produced to date with broadband spectro-polarimetric data in the context of the MeerKAT Fornax Survey and presented in a previous paper (508 sources over 6.35 deg$^2$), we aim to study in detail the Fornax cluster's magnetic field. We compare the RM grid properties with numerical simulations to constrain the strength and the structure of the intra-cluster magnetic field. We model the magnetic field power spectrum with a power-law and we find a slope of $\sim$2.7 fluctuating between $\sim$1 and $\sim$15 kpc. It has a central strength of $\sim$5$μ$G decreasing with the thermal plasma density according to a power-law exponent of $\sim$1.6, the highest value to date in large scale systems. By analysing a sample of 17 galaxy clusters and groups with magnetic field estimates from the literature, we observe larger auto-correlation lengths in the case of massive merging clusters and lower values for relaxed clusters and low-mass systems. We also observe a systematic increase of the central magnetic field strength as a function of central density, $B_0\propto n_0^{0.38}$. Finally, we argue that the steepening of the Fornax cluster's magnetic field profile and its relatively high central strength could be indicative of a recent re-amplification at the centre due to the extended central radio galaxy. The sample analysis supports the proposed scenario, although more detailed magnetic field studies conducted using consistent modelling on larger samples are needed to better understand magnetisation in clusters and groups.

AI.tldr: Using the densest RM grid from the MeerKAT Fornax Survey, the study models the Fornax cluster's magnetic field, revealing strong central fields and power-law behavior, with results indicating that recent central activity may re-amplify magnetic fields; comparisons across clusters suggest cluster mass, dynamical state, and central density influence magnetic properties.
AI.motivation: Magnetic fields in galaxy clusters affect cluster physics and galaxy evolution but are poorly understood due to lack of sensitive, high-resolution spectro-polarimetric data.
AI.method: Utilized the densest RM grid (508 sources over 6.35 deg²) from MeerKAT Fornax Survey broadband spectro-polarimetric data and compared observed rotation measures with numerical simulations to model the intra-cluster magnetic field power spectrum as a power-law.
AI.result: Determined a magnetic field power spectrum slope of ~2.7 with scales between ∼1 and 15 kpc, a central magnetic field strength of ∼5 μG decreasing with thermal plasma density by a power-law exponent of ∼1.6 (highest reported in large scale systems). Found larger auto-correlation lengths in massive merging clusters and lower in relaxed and low-mass clusters, with central magnetic field strength scaling as B₀ ∝ n₀^{0.38}. Proposed that Fornax cluster's magnetic field profile steepening and strong central field indicate recent re-amplification linked to an extended central radio galaxy.
AI.conclusion: The Fornax cluster's magnetic field is stronger and more structured than previously known, possibly due to re-amplification by central radio galaxy activity. Observed trends across clusters highlight the link between cluster state, central density, and magnetic properties. Further consistent magnetic field studies on larger samples are necessary for comprehensive understanding.

title: Latest results from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
comment: Contribution to the 2026 Electroweak session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: The IceCube Neutrino Observatory has opened a new window into the high-energy Universe, providing measurements of neutrinos over a broad energy range. This contribution presents recent results, including a follow-up on the first identification of a steady neutrino source NGC 1068, measurements of the flavor composition of the diffuse astrophysical flux, limits on prompt atmospheric neutrinos, and searches for neutrinos from dark matter annihilation in the Sun. These measurements probe neutrino production mechanisms, fundamental particle interactions, and physics beyond the Standard Model. Looking forward, the recently deployed IceCube Upgrade will enhance sensitivity to lower-energy neutrinos and reduce systematic uncertainties, while the planned IceCube-Gen2 will expand the detector volume, increase the neutrino detection rate, and extend energy reach, enabling more detailed studies of cosmic sources and high-energy particle physics.

AI.tldr: The IceCube Neutrino Observatory has made significant progress in detecting and analyzing high-energy neutrinos, identifying sources like NGC 1068, studying neutrino properties, and searching for dark matter signals. Upcoming upgrades will improve sensitivity and expand research capabilities.
AI.motivation: To explore high-energy neutrino astrophysics and probe fundamental particle interactions and physics beyond the Standard Model using neutrino observations.
AI.method: Utilizing the IceCube Neutrino Observatory to measure neutrinos across a broad energy range, including follow-up studies on identified sources like NGC 1068, flavor composition measurements, and searches for neutrinos from dark matter annihilation; complemented by upgrades to enhance detection capabilities.
AI.result: Identification of a steady neutrino source (NGC 1068), constraints on prompt atmospheric neutrinos, insights into flavor composition of the diffuse flux, and limits on neutrinos from dark matter annihilation; anticipating improved sensitivity and broader energy reach with IceCube Upgrade and IceCube-Gen2.
AI.conclusion: IceCube has provided significant advancements in high-energy neutrino astronomy and particle physics, with future enhancements poised to deepen understanding of cosmic neutrino sources and fundamental physics.

title: Fourth-order galaxy-galaxy-lensing: Theoretical framework and direct estimation
summary: Traditional galaxy-galaxy lensing is a well-established method of probing the statistical properties of the Universe's matter and galaxy distribution. However, this measure does not carry all the statistical information, provided the matter and galaxy distribution contain non-Gaussian features. In order to study these non-Gaussianities, it is necessary to consider higher-order statistical measures. The aim of this work is to extend the analytical basis describing the statistical correlations between galaxies and shear to the fourth order, with special emphasis on the associated aperture statistics. In order to include fourth-order statistics in future analysis of the relation between mass and galaxies, we further investigate whether we can expect to detect these statistics from observations of stage IV surveys. We define the four-point correlation function (4PCF) between the shear and the positions of triplets of foreground galaxies and derive its relation to the respective trispectrum. We convert the 4PCF to aperture statistics and derive the analytical form of the respective filter function, which we then implement in a numerical integration pipeline. Furthermore, we develop a direct estimator that allows us to measure galaxy-mass aperture moments of arbitrary order on pixelized data using a Fast-Fourier-Transform (FFT) algorithm. We show that the corresponding aperture measure $\langle\mathcal{N}^3 M_\mathrm{ap}\rangle$ can be calculated with sub-percent accuracy on relevant aperture scales, $θ$, by means of numerical integration. Furthermore, we apply the FFT-based direct estimator to a mock catalog with a realistic stage IV survey setup on a sky area of $2000~\mathrm{deg}^2$, and detect the connected part of the aperture statistics $\langle\mathcal{N}^3 M_\mathrm{ap}\rangle(θ)$ with a signal-to-noise ratio of roughly nine on small aperture scales.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a method to study fourth-order statistical correlations between galaxies and shear, extending galaxy-galaxy lensing analyses beyond traditional two-point measurements. Using analytical derivations and an FFT-based estimator, the authors demonstrate that these higher-order statistics can be accurately computed and detected in realistic large-scale survey data, revealing non-Gaussian features in galaxy and matter distributions.
AI.motivation: Traditional galaxy-galaxy lensing techniques only capture two-point statistics and thus miss non-Gaussian information crucial for a comprehensive understanding of the matter and galaxy distribution in the Universe. The study aims to incorporate higher-order (fourth-order) statistics to access this additional information.
AI.method: The authors define the four-point correlation function (4PCF) and relate it to the trispectrum, convert it into aperture statistics through derivation of an analytical filter function, implement a numerical integration pipeline for accurate computation, and develop a Fast-Fourier-Transform (FFT) based estimator to measure aperture moments from pixelized data, validated with mock stage IV survey data.
AI.result: The derived aperture measure ⟨N³ M_ap⟩ can be computed with sub-percent accuracy, and the FFT-based estimator applied to a realistic mock survey detects the connected fourth-order aperture statistics with a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately nine on small scales, demonstrating the feasibility of these measurements in stage IV surveys.
AI.conclusion: The paper successfully extends the analytical framework of galaxy-galaxy lensing to include fourth-order statistics, specifically defining and measuring the four-point correlation function between shear and galaxy triplets, enabling the study of non-Gaussian features in galaxy and matter distributions.

title: Probing the 3D Structures of Supernovae through IR Signatures of CO and SiO
summary: We present a new public-domain MOlecular Fitting Analysis Tool (MOFAT) designed to probe molecule-forming regions in supernovae (SNe) through analysis of molecular features in the near- and mid-infrared. MOFAT employs a novel data-driven approach to explore the physical properties of these regions using time-independent radiative transfer simulations that include multidimensional, clump-like structures, constrained by high-precision observations. Such structures are required to reproduce the flux ratio between fundamental and overtone bands, overcoming limitations of traditional one-zone forward-modeling, such as optical-depth effects and initial configurations. Our approach enables spectral fits that can reconstruct overall abundances and temperatures and determine parameterized small-scale structures associated with physical instabilities. We systematically study the relationship between physical parameters and the profiles of CO and SiO, showing that free parameters are constrained, while detection of small-scale structure requires optically thick bands. As a demonstration, MOFAT is applied to SN2024ggi at +285 and +385 days post-explosion. We find that CO formation triggers SiO formation in the inner layers of the CO-rich region previously studied. The inner edge of the SiO-emitting region recedes from velocities of v1 from 1500 to 1000 km/s, indicating continued SiO formation. The SiO mass decreases from about (2-6)E-3 Mo by roughly an order of magnitude, suggesting ongoing evaporation. SiO features indicate clumping, but most of the flux originates from optically thin regions. SiO contributes negligibly to cooling, and we find no evidence for dust formation. Finally, we discuss observational strategies to trace the evolution of molecule formation and its connection to dust formation.

AI.tldr: MOFAT is a new public-domain tool that analyzes infrared molecular features in supernovae using advanced radiative transfer simulations with clumpy structures. Applied to SN2024ggi, it reveals CO-triggered SiO formation, SiO mass changes, and clumping, without dust formation evidence, enhancing understanding of molecule and dust evolution in SNe.
AI.motivation: To probe molecule-forming regions in supernovae by analyzing molecular features in infrared spectra and address limitations of traditional modeling approaches.
AI.method: Developed MOFAT, a data-driven tool employing time-independent radiative transfer simulations with multidimensional, clump-like structures constrained by high-precision observations.
AI.result: Demonstrated MOFAT on SN2024ggi, reconstructing physical parameters, identifying CO-driven SiO formation, observing SiO mass evolution and clumping, and concluding negligible dust formation.
AI.conclusion: MOFAT effectively models molecular regions in supernovae, overcoming prior modeling limitations, providing insights into molecule formation and its relation to dust formation, and enabling improved observational strategies.

title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Trispectrum: I. Estimating the Matter Power Spectrum Covariance with Higher-Order Statistics
comment: 13 pages, 5 figures, 6 appendices. Prepared for submissioin to PRD
summary: We present a method to estimate non-Gaussian power spectrum covariance matrices by directly measuring the response of the small-scale power spectrum to long-wavelength perturbations via bispectrum and trispectrum estimators. Specifically, we derive estimators for the complete non-Gaussian matter power spectrum covariance, including the super-sample contribution, in terms of the squeezed bispectrum and collapsed trispectrum of the underlying density field. We apply these estimators to the Quijote simulations, and recover unbiased estimates of the small-scale ($k\gtrsim 0.15~h/{\rm Mpc}$) matter power spectrum covariance at the percent level using only 25 simulations - comparable to the precision of the sample covariance estimated using 5,000 simulations. This technique significantly reduces the number of simulations needed to estimate power spectrum covariances and opens the possibility of inferring power spectrum covariances directly from survey data, enabling stringent tests of simulations and, potentially, power spectrum analyses that do not rely on external covariance matrices.

AI.tldr: A new method uses bispectrum and trispectrum estimators to efficiently measure non-Gaussian power spectrum covariances, achieving high precision with drastically fewer simulations than traditional approaches.
AI.motivation: Estimating non-Gaussian power spectrum covariance matrices typically requires a large number of simulations, which is computationally expensive.
AI.method: Derive and use estimators based on the squeezed bispectrum and collapsed trispectrum to measure the response of the small-scale power spectrum to long-wavelength perturbations, capturing the complete non-Gaussian covariance including super-sample effects.
AI.result: The method applied to Quijote simulations achieves unbiased small-scale matter power spectrum covariance estimates at percent-level precision using only 25 simulations, matching the accuracy of traditional estimates requiring 5,000 simulations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed bispectrum and trispectrum-based estimators greatly reduce the simulation resources needed to estimate non-Gaussian power spectrum covariances and enable the possibility of inferring these covariances directly from survey data, improving efficiency and enabling new analysis approaches.
